BuildingElementZoneUnconditionedOpaque.description:
Opaque envelope element of an unconditioned zone (e.g. conservatory roof, side wall).

Carries the element's share of H_tr,ue and nothing else. It contributes no solar
gain, because radiation absorbed on an external opaque surface is largely
re-radiated and convected straight back to the environment. There are no thermal
mass fields because thermal mass is not taken into account for unconditioned zones.

u_value.description: U-value (W/m²·K) of the opaque envelope element. Required where the unconditioned zone's method is 'Calculated', whose transmission heat transfer coefficient to the external environment (H_tr,ue) is the sum of (u_value * area) over the envelope elements. The 'Direct' method takes that coefficient as given and does not use it, so it may be omitted there.
u_value.title: U Value

ConservatoryWall.description:
A conservatory wall isn't quite an AbstractWall - it's an ExternalWall on rails + a window on
rails. Nonetheless, like AbstractWalls it does have a building_elements property.
Some variations:
* You can't put doors or windows in a conservatory wall - instead include them as part of
glazing_fraction
* Any vents (mechanical or passive) are part of the wall in general but neither the opaque nor
glazed element specifically. The solid bit of the wall sits underneath the glazed bit of the
wall
* A conservatory wall can be any of the wall_types but external is expected in almost all cases
(a party or sheltered conservatory wall is allowed, albeit unlikely)

Selects the part-load correction factor row in EN 16798-13:2017 Annex B

Input_ZoneUnconditioned.description:
Unconditioned zone (e.g. conservatory, sunspace, attached unheated room).

Carries two things: the heat transfer fields that describe the zone as a whole,
and the zone's own external envelope in building_element. The envelope is used to
compute the solar gains entering the zone, per BS EN ISO 52016-1:2017 Annex E.3.

A building element between a conditioned zone and this unconditioned zone
references it by name through the element's zone_unconditioned field.

method.description: Route used to derive b_ztu for this unconditioned zone. 'Direct': the assessor supplies b_ztu (and optionally H_ztu,tot) explicitly. 'Calculated': b_ztu is derived from the zone's external envelope U-values and ventilation characteristics per ISO 52016-1:2017 section 6.4.5.4.

coeff_temp_limit_unconditioned_zone.description: c_ztu,h,max, the coefficient limiting the assumed temperature in the unconditioned zone (dimensionless, > 0). Caps the zone at a point this fraction of the way from the cooler of the conditioned-zone and outdoor air temperatures to the warmer of the two. The default of 1.0 (ISO 52016-1:2017 Table B.16) caps the zone at the warmer of the two, which it cannot exceed without a heat source of its own. Values above 1.0 allow the zone above that boundary, as required for sunspaces and conservatories with significant solar gains in summer. See BS EN ISO 52016-1:2017 section 6.5.9, Formula 59.
coeff_temp_limit_unconditioned_zone.title: Coeff Temp Limit Unconditioned Zone

factor_adjustment_unconditioned_zone.description: b_ztu, the adjustment factor for the unconditioned zone (dimensionless, strictly between 0 and 1). Required when method is 'Direct'; must be omitted when method is 'Calculated', which derives it from the envelope conductance and ventilation. A value of 1 collapses to the outdoor-air boundary condition (zero buffering); use a building element directly on the conditioned zone for that case rather than an unconditioned zone. See BS EN ISO 52016-1:2017 section 6.4.5.4, Formula 2.
factor_adjustment_unconditioned_zone.title: Factor Adjustment Unconditioned Zone

heat_transfer_coeff_unconditioned_zone_t.description: H_ztu,tot, the total heat transfer coefficient of the unconditioned zone (unit: W/K). Optional when method is 'Direct': omit it and it is derived from b_ztu and the building elements facing the zone, as H_ztc,ztu / (1 - b_ztu). Must be omitted when method is 'Calculated', which also derives it. Exclude thermal bridges from this coefficient: any additional bridges between the unconditioned zone and the external environment are not represented elsewhere. Must exceed the summed H_ztc,ztu of the building elements facing the zone. Supply a value only when it is known independently of b_ztu: the two are not checked against each other, and because b_ztu sets the zone temperature while this coefficient only scales the gains, a value that disagrees with b_ztu changes the gains without raising an error.
heat_transfer_coeff_unconditioned_zone_t.title: Heat Transfer Coeff Unconditioned Zone Total

coeff_ventilation_unconditioned_zone.description: c_ztu,ve, the coefficient expressing the contribution of ventilation to the heat transfer coefficient through the external envelope (dimensionless, >= 0). Applies when method is 'Calculated' and must be omitted when method is 'Direct'. A value of 0 means no ventilation contribution; typical values range from 0 to 10 depending on the air-tightness of the unconditioned zone. When omitted for 'Calculated', core HEM applies its own default of 0.5 from BS EN ISO 52016-1:2017 Table B.5. See section 6.4.5.4, Formula 6.
coeff_ventilation_unconditioned_zone.title: Coeff Ventilation Unconditioned Zone

building_element.description: External envelope of the unconditioned zone (transparent and opaque surfaces exposed to outdoor weather and sun). It supplies the solar gains entering the zone and the areas and transmittances behind the zone's envelope reduction factor (BS EN ISO 52016-1:2017 Formula E.5), and for the 'Calculated' method it is also the sole source of H_tr,ue, the transmission heat transfer coefficient to the external environment, obtained as the sum of (u_value * area) over its elements per ISO 13789:2017 section 7.5. Required and non-empty when method is 'Calculated'. Optional for 'Direct', which takes b_ztu as given and derives H_ztu,tot from it where none is declared, except that it must be declared where a transparent building element of a conditioned zone references this zone, and at least one transparent element is required when coeff_temp_limit_unconditioned_zone is greater than 1.
building_element.title: Building Element

SpaceCoolSystemHeatPumpAir.description:
Cool air distribution served by a reversible heat pump (EN 16798-13 Method 2).
The heat pump (referenced in $.HeatSourceWet) conditions air directly and
delivers it to the zone, optionally through a ducted distribution fan; the
chilled-water alternative is SpaceCoolSystemHeatPumpFanCoil. The operating
EER is computed from the heat pump's nominal EER, the outdoor temperature,
and the part-load ratio; compressor electricity is settled on the heat
pump's energy supply, and any ducted distribution fan on the energy supply
named here.

non-conditioned space (loft, garage, void) loses that heat from the
dwelling.

hem_epc_orchestrator__models__epc__FlueC.description:
Flue configuration for a combustion appliance.

Identifies the flue type of the appliance, and — for open-flue variants —
links the appliance to the passive or hybrid duct that models its flue
and provides the fuel-flow factor used to compute combustion air flow
while it is firing (BS EN 16798-7:2017 §6.4.3.4, eq. 35).

The room-sealed variant is also accepted so that the flue type can be
recorded on every combustion appliance, even when there is no flue
contribution to the dwelling ventilation. This collects the data needed
to make ``flue_type`` mandatory in a later release. The flueless variant
is rejected, since a flueless appliance has no flue to configure.

Open-flue variants (OPEN_FLUE, CHIMNEY): the duct reference and
fuel-flow factor are both required. The room-sealed variant: both
must be omitted.

PassiveDuct.description: Name of the passive or hybrid duct that models this appliance's flue. References a key in $.InfiltrationVentilation.PassiveDucts. Required for open-flue variants; omit for room-sealed.
PassiveDuct.title: Passiveduct

fuel_flow_factor.description: Combustion air flow per unit fuel input power (unit: l/s/kW). Used in BS EN 16798-7:2017 eq. 35 to compute the combustion air flow while the appliance is firing. Some default values are tabulated in BS EN 16798-7:2017 Table B.3. Required for open-flue variants; omit for room-sealed.
fuel_flow_factor.title: Fuel Flow Factor

hem_epc_orchestrator__models__epc__FlueG.description:
Flue Gas Heat Recovery System with thermal storage, coupled to a combi boiler.

Captures heat from the flue gas during boiler firing into a small (typically
25-50 L) thermal store and uses it to preheat the cold-mains feed during hot
water draw-offs. All four heat-transfer conductances are required and must
be obtained directly from BS EN 13203-7 testing.

The M-factor approximation (estimating h_charge_hw from the space-heating
charging coefficient scaled by the boiler output ratio) is intentionally
not supported: it can under-estimate h_charge_hw by approximately 30%
relative to the directly-measured value, depending on the device.
